items.summary: Irdina Auni, editor of The Pride and Singapore Kindness Movement, opens a forum post asking whether money can motivate good habits like recycling or reading. She cites the 2025 Graciousness Survey by the Singapore Kindness Movement as showing strong belief in kindness that does not always become action. Weighing Self-Determination Theory's crowding-out effect against practical barriers and recognition, she concludes no: kindness is too important to be reduced to a transaction.
items.title: Singapore editor rejects paying for kindness

items.summary: The Ministry of Health thanked Tan Chu Quan for her October 26 letter proposing that prenatal medical expenses be deducted directly from MediSave before childbirth. Director Justin How said officials will study allowing MediSave use as and when such expenses are incurred, noting the current MediSave Maternity Package already covers up to $900 for pre-delivery costs on top of applicable withdrawal limits.
items.title: MOH to study direct MediSave deductions for prenatal medical expenses

items.summary: Renault Group plans an autonomous electric vehicle platform called Forefront, co-developed with Belgian firm John Cockerill for demanding Armée de Terre missions. CEO François Provost says the modular concept previews unmanned ground vehicles usable in civilian and military sectors over coming years. The project combines Renault's mass production strength with Cockerill's defense expertise. Prototypes are still a rendering, with trials planned to refine it.
items.title: Renault Partners With John Cockerill On Autonomous Military Vehicle

items.summary: AI firms are increasingly partnering with oil and gas companies, according to reporting from Reuters, Semafor, and the Wall Street Journal. OpenAI signed a deal with Abu Dhabi's ADNOC this Monday, while Nvidia announced plans for a large fossil-fuel plant in Ohio, and Microsoft agreed to a 20-year contract with Chevron for natural-gas power. Experts warn these ties may increase emissions.
items.title: Big Tech's Fossil Fuel Deals Deepen

items.summary: A weekly tech roundup reports that Anthropic’s amended IPO filing lists $437.4B in non-cancellable commitments, including $69.8B due within 12 months, while Q3 revenue grew 46.9% and compute costs rose 77.4%. The piece notes Nasdaq fell more than 10% below its October record on November 5 as chipmakers and AI names led the selloff. Separately, Menlo Ventures puts enterprise AI deployment spend at $176.8B, up from $33B a year earlier, with frontier labs taking 69% of it. Sequoia said it is closing its London office after raising roughly $10B in new funds.
items.title: Anthropic Discloses $437.4B in Commitments as Nasdaq Enters Correction

items.summary: Bailiffs acting for Jaguar Land Rover raided the Dutch offices of Chinese carmaker BYD in August, seizing digital records ahead of a court case this week over whether its Ti7 SUV infringes the intellectual property rights of the Land Rover Defender. Motoring experts have likened the seven-seat plug-in hybrid to the Defender since it went on sale in China last September. JLR and BYD declined to comment on the ongoing legal proceedings, which follow earlier copycat disputes involving Jiangling Motor Corporation and Chery's Jaecoo model.
items.title: JLR Bailiffs Raid BYD Dutch Offices Over Defender Clone Claim

items.summary: A new CIEL analysis says British company Ineos is leading growth in the export of US-fracked ethane used for European plastics. Data analysed by CIEL shows volumes shipped by or for Ineos rose roughly 7.3-fold from 2016, growing from 429 kilotonnes to 3,130 kilotonnes by 2025, with the company responsible for at least two-thirds of US ethane exports. Campaigner Lois Bower-Bjornson blames her children's health problems on nearby fracking wells and says Project One in Antwerp will depend on this gas. Ineos denies owning Pennsylvania wells and disputes that a single project drives the trade.
items.title: CIEL analysis reveals Ineos leads US fracked ethane trade to Europe

items.summary: कर्णाटक सरकार ने दवा किया है कि कहीं सैंपल में 31.2% तक इथानॉल मिला। IOCL, BPCL और HPCL ने इन आरोपों को खारिज करते हुए BIS मानक IS 17021 के अनुरूप पेट्रोल तैयार किया जा रहा है कहा है और सैंपल व लैब रिपोर्ट उपलब्ध नहीं करायी गई पर चुनौती उठायी है।
items.title: तेल कंपनियों और कर्नाटक सरकार बीच ई20 पेट्रोल में इथेनॉल विवाद पर सफाई

items.summary: Brokerage firm Samco Securities named ten Indian stocks, including Adani Power and Tech Mahindra, as potential Muhurat Trading picks for the start of new fiscal year 2083 in November 2026. It expects up to 110% returns over a year on some names but advised investors to watch profits and stop losses.
items.title: Samco Securities names 10 stocks for Diwali trading gains

items.summary: A Quartz report, illustrated by NPR data, examines spending in the 2026 U.S. midterms. Total cycle spending reached nearly $12 billion, described as the most expensive election cycle yet, ahead of even the 2024 presidential race. The article notes a tension: heavy ad spending may not translate into results. Spending did not flow evenly; much favored outside groups aligned with Republicans and moved through super PACs. Seven high-cost races are highlighted, including Texas Senate (Paxton vs. Talarico), Michigan Senate (Rogers vs. El-Sayed), California governor ($349.4 million in primary spending), North Carolina's 1st District, New York's 17th District, and Florida's 25th District—each passing $50 million in ad spending for the first time. Several outcomes could not be independently confirmed when written; disputed totals were left out rather than guessed. The record can be read against NPR's argument that political ads have limited effect.
items.title: Record Midterm Spending and Six High-Cost Races

items.summary: Two people were arrested after an influencer boxing event in Kilkenny, Ireland, descended into a riot on Saturday. The disorder followed the presence of far-right activist Tommy Robinson (Stephen Yaxley-Lennon), 43, who was a ringside guest at the event organised by HSTikkyTokky and Ed Matthews under their Unhinged events company. Tensions rose when Robinson made inflammatory comments about Muslims before competitor Mo Deen's fight; after Deen won, he confronted Robinson, prompting organiser Sullivan to demand a bareknuckle rematch that escalated into violence involving chairs, barricades and punches. A man in his 30s was assaulted and taken to St Luke's hospital, while another male in his 20s was arrested. There is no suggestion the riot was pre-planned. Sullivan later acknowledged he had erred by not hiring more security.
items.title: Riot Erupts at Irish Influencer Boxing Event After Tommy Robinson's Presence

items.summary: A surgeon treating victims after a mass shooting in Krakow, Poland said his colleague undoubtedly saved the life of a gravely injured police officer. The two doctors were eating near Main Market Square on Saturday when a gunman began firing at random, killing six and injuring 15. They treated both the attacker and officers shot while subduing him; both emerged from comas Sunday. Prosecutors launched a terror investigation after ministers said the 24-year-old attacker was inspired by far-right ideologies.
items.title: Kraków Surgeon Says Colleague Saved Officer's Life After Mass Shooting

items.summary: Culture secretary Lisa Nandy said she wants to avoid “circular arguments” about whether the UK should rejoin the EU, underlining divisions at the top of government over revisiting Brexit. She appeared not in favour of rejoining but said the prime minister should still pursue closer ties. Cabinet colleagues privately warned Burnham’s plan could reopen a row benefiting Reform UK. Nandy rejected allegations that celebrating Erasmus plus before Remembrance Sunday was inappropriate, telling Sky News: “I cannot see what is political about saying that we want young people from every part of this country to understand the contribution.”
items.title: Lisa Nandy wary of circular arguments over rejoining EU

items.summary: At least seven people died in a train collision near the Egyptian city of Giza, with more than 100 injured. The country's railway authority said two trains travelling south collided, derailing carriages that fell down an embankment. President Abdul Fattah al-Sisi ordered authorities to investigate and hold negligent parties accountable, while hospitals were placed on heightened alert amid a large influx of patients.
items.title: Egypt Train Collision Leaves Seven Dead and Over 100 Injured Near Giza

items.summary:
New Zealanders will wait for weeks after Saturday's election failed to deliver a decisive win, leaving negotiations over a wafer-thin governing majority as the only path forward. The tightest vote in years rebuked both Luxon's center-right National party and Chris Hipkins's Labour by boosting minor parties on the ideological flanks. New entrant Opportunity won seven seats under leader Qiulae Wong, frustrating either bloc. Conservative incumbent Luxon did not claim victory but urged calm while leading a caretaker government until final tallies are released Nov. 27. With National holding just 67 of 131 seats and special votes historically favoring the left, no side can govern alone without cross-bloc support.

visual null
items.title: New Zealand election produces no clear winner amid weeks of talks

items.summary: Police searched an empty Main Market Square in Kraków on Nov 8 as Poland entered two days of mourning after a gunman killed six people and wounded 15, including two police officers. Authorities called it Poland's deadliest gun rampage in decades. Investigators found the suspect's parents and sister dead at his home. Interior Minister Marcin Kierwinski said the shooter appeared fascinated by far-right ideologies. A terrorism investigation was launched as citizens expressed grief and solidarity.
items.title: Poland Mourns Deadly Kraków Mass Shooting Amid Far-Right Fears

items.summary: Pascal Gross dismissed Brighton & Hove Albion's Premier League title credentials on Sunday despite a 2-0 home victory over Brentford that lifted the club to second in the table. Fabian Huerzeler's side have 22 points from 10 games, five adrift of champions Arsenal. Gross said they are not getting carried away yet and must keep improving through fixtures after the international break.
items.title: Brighton's Pascal Gross Downplays Title Hopes After Strong Start

items.summary: South Africa's African National Congress (ANC) secured less than 31% of the vote in Wednesday's municipal polls, its worst-ever result. The Electoral Commission said on Saturday it lost majorities in six of eight metropolitan regions, forcing coalition talks. ANC Secretary-General Fikile Mbalula called the outcome catastrophic and blamed declining public trust amid corruption and service failures.
items.title: ANC Records Worst-Ever Election Result in South Africa

items.summary: About 200 former Bathla workers are demanding answers over unpaid wages and entitlements, some saying they were owed tens of thousands of dollars. Jagdeep Singh has estimated he is owed $80,000 after nine years at the Sydney developer, which entered voluntary administration in August owing at least $3. 4 billion. Teneo's senior managing director Andrew Scott put employee-related creditor claims at around $6 million, covering wages, superannuation and leave only. For temporary visa holders like Arjun and Kelly, job loss risks their right to remain in Australia; they are ineligible for the Fair Entitlements Guarantee while Bathla remains in administration rather than liquidation. The NSW Supreme Court has extended the deadline for administrators until September 2027. Insolvency expert Jason Harris said employees retain rights to employment records even during administration, and workers may raise concerns with the Fair Work Ombudsman.
items.title: Bathla Workers Demand Answers Over Unpaid Wages Amid Insolvency

items.summary: Political analysts are weighing whether President Donald Trump will fire Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, framing it partly as a media opportunity rather than policy. Tom Popinsky of Cornell University suggested the president might treat a dismissal like an episode of The Apprentice to boost television ratings and make news. Hegseth faces criticism over his support for military intervention in Iran and other decisions, while Democrats who will control Congress from January have signaled plans to impeach him; Colorado Democrat Jason Crow said he is 'going after Pete Hegseth.' Hegseth dismissed the pressure as political theatre. Popinsky called the situation 'norm breaking of the highest level,' though he noted it remains impossible to know whether a firing would occur.
items.title: Analysts weigh Trump firing Hegseth as ratings play

items.summary: The recently concluded Fifth Plenary Session of the 20th CPC Central Committee reaffirmed its 'Three Nos' anti-corruption strategy: officials should not dare to be corrupt, should not be able to be corrupt, and ultimately should not want to be corrupt. The article explains each line as a defense—making corruption costly, harder to commit, and ethically undesirable—with the shared goal of keeping public power in check.
items.title: China's CPC Frames Anti-Corruption Strategy as Three Interlocking Principles

items.summary: This piece previews an episode examining how the Communist Party of China sustains effectiveness after decades in power. It identifies two official answers: supervision by the people and self-revolution, both reaffirmed at the Fifth Plenary Session of the 20th CPC Central Committee. The discussion turns on converting periodic campaigns into lasting institutional practice.
items.title: CPC Frames Self-Revolution as Enduring Party Renewal Strategy

items.summary: A car plunged into a rural lake in Barra Mansa, Rio de Janeiro state, killing at least ten people, including five children. The government of the state confirmed the death toll and said the victims were already dead when recovered by firefighters with two divers' help. Brazilian media say a baby was among them, though identities remain unconfirmed. Local authorities called it an accident while police investigate; heavy rain had caused flooding across the region earlier.
items.title: Brazilian car plunge into lake kills ten, including five children

items.summary:
Azerbaijan marked its sixth Victory Day on Sunday, commemorating the end of the 2020 Karabakh war. President Ilham Aliyev led ceremonies in Khankendi and Shusha, laying a wreath at the Victory Monument. Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan joined the commemorations by invitation to signal bilateral strength despite recent diplomatic disagreements between Ankara and Baku. Both leaders reaffirmed their alliance during a joint press conference; Aliyev declared "this unity will last forever." The article notes reconstruction progress in regained territories, with 97,000 people now living there under the Great Return Programme, over €10 billion in state infrastructure spending since 2020, and plans for green energy. It also outlines Azerbaijan's ongoing peace process with Armenia and regional economic integration efforts.

visual":{"decision":"none","why":"The item is a narrative news report about a diplomatic visit and commemorations; it conveys events, quotes and context rather than quantitative comparisons that a chart would clarify.
items.title: Azerbaijan's Victory Day marks sixth anniversary of Karabakh war end

items.summary: South Africa's local government elections on November 4, 2026 marked the worst electoral performance for the ruling African National Congress (ANC), which secured approximately 30.8% of the vote according to results published by the Independent Electoral Commission (IEC). The Democratic Alliance obtained close to 24.6%, while the uMkhonto weSizwe Party gained about 9.8%. With no party securing an outright majority in roughly 120 municipal councils, political parties have begun negotiations under a legally prescribed 14-day period to form governing coalitions. Analyst Xolelwa Kashe-Katiya warned that rushed talks could produce fragile administrations affecting service delivery and infrastructure projects across municipalities.
items.title: South African Local Elections Force Coalition Building After ANC Weakness

items.summary: The Iranian American Legal Defense Fund alleges the Trump administration removed 11 Iranian nationals at about 4:00 a.m. on Sunday, November 8, 2026, via Pakistan in an overnight operation that it claims violated a federal court order requiring five business days' advance notice before removals to Iran or a coordinating third country. The group filed the emergency motion after learning of the plan Saturday evening; whether the charter flight departed as scheduled remains unconfirmed.
items.title: Rights group says US deported 11 Iranians without court-ordered notice

items.summary: French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot announced that Europe will take part in the upcoming Abu Dhabi peace talks on ending the Ukraine war, mediated by the United States. The summit is scheduled for Tuesday and Wednesday, following a Brussels meeting attended by American, European, Ukrainian and NATO officials. France stated it would ensure Europe's voice was heard at the negotiations.
items.title: France Confirms European Participation in US-Mediated Ukraine Talks

items.summary: The African National Congress topped South Africa's local elections on Saturday but recorded its worst-ever result, winning just 32.5% of the vote while dropping roughly 14 percentage points from 2021. Frustrated voters shifted toward the Democratic Alliance and smaller lists, leaving no party with an outright majority in any metropolitan municipality and pointing to complex coalition negotiations ahead.
items.title: ANC wins South Africa local polls amid record-low vote share

items.summary: New Zealand's National Party-led coalition won a narrow majority in Saturday's general election, with the NZ Herald reporting all 131 seats counted as of November 8, 2026. The alliance secured 67 seats—one more than needed—putting Christopher Luxon on course for a second term. Opposition Labour, Green and Maori parties won 57 seats. Results may shift when about 700,000 special votes are counted by November 27.
items.title: Luxon Positioned for Second Term After Narrow Coalition Win

items.summary:
Employees at some Disney divisions received an email cancelling their annual Halloween celebration, sparking fears of more layoffs even as the industry enjoys one of its best years at the box office. Netflix recently laid off around 1,000 employees, roughly 6% of its workforce. Paramount's acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery to form Skydance is worth nearly $100 billion and has sparked anxiety about future cuts. An Ernst & Young study found U. S. film production budgets fell from 74% to 42%, with Los Angeles losing ground amid rising labor costs. Meanwhile, summer ticket sales reached $5 billion in 2026, driven by films like The Odyssey and Spider-Man. Yet Hollywood remains clouded by uncertainty as mergers loom over the industry's future.

items.title: Disney Layoffs and Mergers Cloud Hollywood Despite Box Office Boom

items.summary: The Japanese government conducted a three-day nuclear emergency drill simulating a severe accident at Hokkaido Electric Power's Tomari plant. About 8,500 residents are expected to participate, and Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi declared a nuclear emergency during the exercise. The scenario involves an earthquake disabling No. 3 reactor cooling; that reactor met new safety standards in 2025, though its restart timing remains uncertain amid court proceedings.
items.title: Japan Runs Nuclear Emergency Drill at Tomari Plant for First Time in a Decade

items.summary: A Japanese employee of Astellas Pharma, sentenced to three years and six months for espionage in China, is expected to be released around Dec. 14 and return to Japan, sources said Saturday. He was detained by Chinese authorities in March 2023 while leaving after his Beijing assignment and indicted in August 2024.
items.title: Japanese Astellas Employee Expected Release From China Prison in December

items.summary: Elon Musk announced Tesla will stop building the Cybertruck at its Texas Gigafactory around mid-2027 to free space for Cybercab robotaxis. The truck fell far short of expectations: Cox Automotive estimates 20,237 US sales in 2025, down 48% from 38,965 in 2024. Musk's SpaceX bought $131 million worth last year at full price. Tesla shares rose over 4% on the news.
items.title: Tesla To End Cybertruck Production By Mid-2027, Musk Says

items.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi said on Sunday that although armed Naxalites had been eliminated from the forests, the threat of Naxalism remained. He claimed 'Dimagi Naxals' had taken control of several organisations including political parties and urged the country to identify and defeat such elements to ensure national security. His remarks follow a March 31 announcement by the Centre that it had freed the country from Naxalism.
items.title: Modi Warns Dimagi Naxals Threaten National Security

items.summary: A confrontation outside TMC leader Abhishek Banerjee's Kalighat residence in Kolkata has triggered a political feud between the Trinamool Congress and BJP. Mamata Banerjee joined his protest, accusing the ruling party of hooliganism and writing to Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla over law-and-order concerns. The clash reportedly began around 2 am after BJP supporters allegedly raised slogans outside his home; Abhishek claimed it continued until 7 am while police said initial clashes lasted about two hours. Both sides traded accusations, with the BJP blaming a public birthday gathering and TMC leaders alleging surveillance and assault. Police imposed prohibitory orders and detained people as investigations continue against a backdrop of shifting power in Bengal after the 2026 Assembly elections ended the TMC's rule.
items.title: Bengal clash over Abhishek Banerjee's birthday protest sparks BJP-TMC row

items.summary: Confidential records obtained by Belarusian group Cyber Partisans and Ukrainian operation Silent Crow show that Russia has recorded the deaths of about 400,000 of its people fighting in Ukraine since the full-scale invasion almost five years ago. The figures come from more than 11 million death certificates held by Rosstat’s statistics agency, with nearly 392,700 explicitly linked to the war between Feb. 24, 2022 and late August 2026. Bloomberg News reviewed the material after it was shared with a small group of outlets. The data almost certainly understates total fatalities because combat deaths are hard to record; Silent Crow’s own estimate is about 450,000. Rosstat did not respond to requests for comment and denied its databases were compromised despite reporting cyberattacks in late October and early November 2026.
items.title: Hacked Rosstat Data Reveals Russia’s War Death Toll

items.summary: This article traces Jeff Bezos's real estate growth, opening with his 1994 move into a Bellevue house rented for $890 a month. It then outlines how Amazon expanded and describes later acquisitions across Texas, New York, California, Washington DC and Hawaii, ending on the theme of an estimated portfolio now worth more than $700 million. The Times of India states it has not independently verified the property details or prices mentioned.
items.title: Jeff Bezos's journey from $890 rental to $700m property empire

items.summary: Chief Minister D K Shivakumar sought Tamil Nadu's cooperation, not permission, for the proposed Mekedatu balancing reservoir across Cauvery river at Mekedatu in Kanakapura. He said it would benefit Bengaluru drinking water and Tamil Nadu more than Karnataka, with a pumped-storage component generating 400 MW of electricity while submerging around 5,400 hectares of forest land. Karnataka's Supreme Court order favouring the state stands; Vijay opposes it.
items.title: Karnataka CM seeks Tamil Nadu cooperation for Mekedatu project

items.summary: Corporate executives are accelerating mergers and acquisitions as midterm losses raise fears that a resurgent Democratic Congress could scrutinize or block large transactions. Kevin Foley of JPMorgan Chase & Co. warns companies should be ready to transact, while Fernando Rivas of Wells Fargo & Co. describes a returning “now or never” mentality. Analysis of Bloomberg-compiled data shows more than half of announced US deals worth at least $50 billion over two decades occurred under Trump’s presidency. Recent megadeals include Marvell Technology Inc.’s record-breaking $100 billion takeover of Lumentum Holdings Inc., Paramount Skydance Corp.’s $110 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery Inc., DoorDash Inc.’s $17 billion purchase of Maplebear Inc., and NextEra Energy Inc.’s $67 billion buy of Dominion Energy Inc. Paul Nary of the University of Pennsylvania’s Wharton School advises announcing deals by mid-2027, noting “There isn’t that much time left.”
items.title: Wall Street Dealmakers Race for Megadeals Amid Trump-Era Countdown

items.summary: Osarugue Otebele, an Assistant Professor at the University of Toronto, argues that South Korean TV series repeatedly portray Africa as a place for character-building, rebellion or punishment. In her study she traced this pattern across three shows including Queen of Tears (2024), which ranked 14th most watched on Netflix by 2024. She suggests these depictions help South Korea define its rising soft power against an image of Africa as savage and lacking. Drawing on Achille Mbembe's work, she links the trope to how nations distinguish themselves through contrast with Africa, noting it now extends beyond Western colonial powers to eastern economies like China and South Korea.
items.title: Scholar examines Africa's role in K-dramas and Hallyu Wave

items.summary: A major fire engulfed a garage near Prime Academy School on Marol Military Road in Andheri East, Mumbai, late Sunday night. The Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation’s Disaster Management Cell reported the blaze at 10.51 pm and classified it as Level-II (major). Firefighting operations continued into the early hours with the Mumbai Fire Brigade, police personnel and ward staff deployed to the scene. No injuries have been reported so far, a fire official confirmed, while the cause remains unknown.
items.title: Mumbai Fire Brigade Battles Major Garage Blaze on Marol Military Road

items.summary: Bollywood celebrities marked Diwali with family celebrations, sharing traditional festive attire and photographs from their personal gatherings. A star couple shared their first family photograph with their newborn child for the occasion. These posts gave fans an insight into how film personalities celebrated the festival.
items.title: Bollywood Stars Share Diwali Family Moments

items.summary: The Mankhurd police registered an FIR against three men for allegedly setting a sky lantern on fire with an inflammable substance and releasing it in public. Two of the men were detained; their friend, Shahrukh, reportedly flew the burning lantern before fleeing when spotted at around 1.20 am on November 5 near Sahyadri Gym. The device landed on a house roof but burned out on its own. All three have been booked under Sections 287, 125 and 223 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita. Further investigation is underway.
items.title: Mumbai Police Book Three Men Over Sky Lantern Fire Risk

items.summary: Madhya Pradesh International Master Anuj Shrivatri became India's 100th Grandmaster after winning the 7th ASEAN Plus Individual Open Chess Championship on Sunday. The 22-year-old scored seven out of eight points, losing only the first game at a complex in Misamis Occidental. Earlier GMs Ethan Vaz, Harshvardhan GB, S Ashwath and V Rathnavel had received titles between July and November 2026.
items.title: Chess Player Anuj Shrivatri Becomes India's 100th Grandmaster After Championship Win in the Philippines

items.summary: The BJP targeted Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge over his description of Diwali as 'Khushiyon Ka Eid', calling him 'anti-Sanatan' and accusing the party of appeasement politics. Spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari posted the charge on X, while Sudhanshu Trivedi accused Congress of sympathy toward Mughal ruler Babur. The row revived controversy over former president Sonia Gandhi's 1992 remarks about the Babri Masjid demolition.
items.title: Congress is anti-Sanatan: BJP targets Kharge over Diwali 'Khushiyon ka Eid' remark

items.summary: An explainer by Arshdeep Kaur of Mint describes how Diwali is observed differently across India, framed as a festival celebrating light over darkness. The piece surveys regional customs: Sikhs mark Bandi Chhor Divas to commemorate Guru Hargobind's release from Gwalior Fort along with 52 Rajput princes; Gujarat ties the festival to Bestu Varas and Chopda Pujan of new account books; West Bengal observes Kali Puja focused on destroying evil rather than wealth; Goa stages effigies of Narakasura before a festive breakfast of poha. Tamil Nadu celebrates Naraka Chaturdashi, Maharashtra holds Govatsa Dwadashi honouring cows, Karnataka marks Bali Padyami for King Bali's return, and Varanasi lights 84 ghats on Kartik Purnima, 15 days after Diwali.
items.title: Diwali traditions vary across Indian states and communities

items.summary: Delhi's air quality reached 'very poor' status on Sunday, with AQI at 371 by 7pm per the Central Pollution Control Board. Of 59 monitoring stations, 20 recorded 'severe' levels and Jahangirpuri topped the list at 464. Firecrackers drove PM2.5 pollution, though forecasts warn conditions may worsen from November 9 as weather hampers pollutant dispersion.
items.title: Delhi Air Quality Hits Very Poor Levels Amid Diwali Firecrackers

items.summary: Gadi Eisenkot, chairman of the Yashar party, officially received a mandate from President Isaac Herzog to form Israel's next government. The decision followed presidential consultations in which factions representing 67 Members of the Knesset recommended Eisenkot while representatives of 46 lawmakers backed Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. Under the mandate, Eisenkot has 28 days to negotiate and form a coalition, with Herzog able to grant up to 14 additional days if required. A faction of seven lawmakers abstained from recommending either candidate. The main obstacle is disagreement over whether the government could rely on Arab-led parties; Yisrael Beiteinu's Avigdor Liberman has ruled out such support and faces accusations of obstructing Eisenkot for personal ambitions, which he denied.
items.title: Eisenkot Given Mandate To Form Israeli Government

items.summary: Israel's defence minister Israel Katz said on Sunday that the campaign against Iran is far from over, reported AFP. He warned Hezbollah to stay out of renewed fighting and repeated claims that Tehran seeks nuclear weapons, which Iran denies. Netanyahu faces domestic pressure after losing ground in his October 27 election, with rival Gadi Eisenkot tasked forming a government. Katz said Israel will not withdraw from the security zones in Gaza, Lebanon and Syria.
items.title: Israel's Defence Minister Says Iran Campaign Is Far From Over

items.summary: The Kerala High Court directed the Special Investigation Team probing alleged irregularities in procurement and supply of Milma ghee to Sabarimala to pursue all relevant leads and examine every person who may have played a role, irrespective of official position. The bench expressed satisfaction that the probe was proceeding properly but urged thoroughness and impartiality.
items.title: Probe everyone's involvement on irregularities in Milma ghee supply to Sabarimala: HC to SIT

items.summary: Karnataka Chief Minister D K Shivakumar said petrol samples had been tested at 67 locations across the state after motorists complained of reduced mileage and engines stalling. He cited complaints that 31.5 per cent ethanol was being blended into petrol, saying the government took them seriously and notified the central government. A ministerial press conference is scheduled for Monday to release details.
items.title: Karnataka Chief Minister Orders Petrol Sample Tests After Ethanol Blending Complaints

items.summary: During Deepavali, Tamil Nadu recorded one child death and 269 firecracker-related burn treatments over a 24-hour window ending 7 am on November 8. The state 108 ambulance network logged 16,079 calls; government hospitals admitted 1,387 patients (956 accidents, 321 minor injuries or assaults, 110 burns). Men were the largest burn group (92 outpatients, 76 inpatients), followed by children under 15. The Thanjavur Government Medical College Hospital handled the highest volume of cases.
items.title: Tamil Nadu Firecracker Burn Toll During Diwali

items.summary: Karnataka Chief Minister Shivakumar alleges excessive ethanol blending in motor spirit, saying thousands of vehicles face engine failures and reduced mileage. He says mixing occurs at petrol bunks and the Centre has been informed about 67 locations where samples were collected; an investigation is underway with about 30 per cent complete. The state's Department of Food, Civil Supplies, Consumer Affairs and Legal Metrology claimed spirit contained between 26 per cent and 31 per cent ethanol. Three Oil Marketing Companies say blending is automated under statutory guidelines.
items.title: Karnataka CM Alleges Excessive Ethanol Blending Amid Fuel Complaints

items.summary: The Men's Selection Committee added Ayush Badoni to India A's updated 15-member squad for the ACC Rising Stars Asia Cup, replacing Patidar. Rinku Singh serves as deputy captain under Tilak Varma. The committee noted that Patidar informed the BCCI he should not be considered for selection in the 50-over format while managing his injuries.
items.title: Rinku Singh named India A vice-captain

items.summary: Mihir Chitre's Screenwriters Inc., published by Om Books International, collects 33 lockdown-era interviews with Indian film writers for the Hindustan Times. The author frames it as a way to correct popular ignorance about screenwriting, noting that many interviewees were unfamiliar even though their films were well known. He observes that screenwriting was long treated as an add-on rather than a profession and highlights how gender and queer themes have shifted attitudes since the 1980s and '90s. The book avoids taking sides among differing views on cinema's purpose, aiming instead to give writers greater visibility.
items.title: A book brings Indian screenwriters into focus through interviews
